name: rigid_vessel_water_heat_removal
title: Rigid 50 L vessel: heat removed from water at constant volume (exercise)
summary: Teaching exercise for a closed rigid 50 L vessel of water at 120 °C and quality 0.6. The model computes the mass, the final quality at the temperature stored in the equation window, and the heat removed at constant volume.

verification.summary: Against the stored solution of R2_E1_2022.EES, compare_solution.py --ees-units reports: 12 common variables, 2 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 1; only in CoolSolve: 0. The maximum over all common variables is 9.65e-01 on T_f. T_i and T_f stay 393.15 K and 283.15 K; the tool rewrites those kelvin values to °C. Q is -155559 J (stored -155.539 kJ), m_eau is 0.0934315 kg and x_f is 0.00502483.
verification.reference: EES stored solution in R2_E1_2022.EES (13 variables, EES X10.836), compared with compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: Largest relative difference printed by compare_solution.py --ees-units is 9.65e-01 on T_f. T_i prints 6.95e-01. The equation window stores T_i = 393.15 K and T_f = 283.15 K, and the model keeps those kelvin values. The tool subtracts 273.15 from a stored kelvin value whose name starts with T and compares 393.15 with 120 and 283.15 with 10. Q prints 1.26e-04 (-155558.556 J against the stored -155.5389041 kJ). m_eau prints 1.27e-04 (0.093431492 kg against 0.093419626 kg). x_f prints 1.64e-05 (0.005024835 against 0.005024752), inside the dome. u_i prints 6.27e-07 and u_f and u_f_bis print 6.61e-07; both final internal energies are equal, and Q stays inside rtol. The only name present in EES alone is x = 0 m^2, which is not in the equation window. 0 iterations with .initials and 0 without. All 12 equations are satisfied (max residual 0). The quality() warning that v looks like a density is cosmetic; v_i is a specific volume.
